title: ChatGPT for Good? On Opportunities and Challenges of Large Language Models for Education
extended_summary:
This position paper examines the opportunities and challenges of large language models, especially ChatGPT and related GPT-style systems, for education. Rather than reporting an empirical study, the authors synthesize early research and offer a conceptual overview of how these models may support learning and teaching, while also identifying major risks and governance concerns.

The paper discusses student-facing uses such as generating quizzes, flashcards, summaries, explanations, reading-comprehension questions, tutoring support, and language-learning assistance. It also discusses teacher-facing uses such as lesson planning, adaptive feedback, assessment support, exercise generation, and professional development. The discussion spans elementary, middle/high school, university, remote learning, and professional learning contexts, with special attention to language learning, reading comprehension, writing, and problem solving.

The main conclusion is that large language models can improve personalization, efficiency, and access to instructional resources, but only if they are used with strong human oversight, curriculum alignment, fact-checking, bias mitigation, privacy protections, and clear pedagogical strategies. The paper emphasizes that these systems are not replacements for teachers and should be integrated as complementary tools within responsible educational design.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-based large language model chatbot for generating, answering, and revising natural language text.
identified_tools.use_case: Discussed as a general-purpose LLM for education; the paper highlights potential uses for reading comprehension support, quiz generation, summaries, explanations, feedback, lesson planning, and assessment, but does not report an empirical classroom study of ChatGPT itself.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a position paper, not an empirical evaluation. It offers conceptual discussion and recommendations rather than a study with measured outcomes or implementation data.
impact_tier_rationale: No outcome data, effect sizes, or classroom impact measures are reported, so there is no basis for estimating impact from this paper.
